beats.care: Complaints can go to the WhatsApp group with officials. In an emergency, dial 112.
beats.what: Students from LSR, Gargi, Maitreyi, JMC and other colleges met CM Rekha Gupta on Monday. They flagged Siri Fort Road, Mukherjee Nagar and metro stations.
beats.why: Students say poor lighting, few patrols and long walks to buses make evenings risky.

cards.body: Students asked for safety audits of dark spots, more pink booths and women police, more patrols and more DTC buses with stops near remote colleges.
The CM asked students to use it in any emergency. Unsolved complaints can go to senior police.
cards.caption: Emergency number

cards.body: Problem spots weren't just campuses: metro stations, bridges and PG-heavy streets were named too.

cards.q: What would make your commute feel safer?
What was promised to keep students in touch with officials?
cards.why: The CM said a WhatsApp group linking students and officials will stay active.

hook: Which Delhi spots do *college women* say feel unsafe?

learn.t: Delhi is installing about 1 lakh smart streetlights linked to its Integrated Command and Control Centre.

sources.name: The Statesman
sources.title: Delhi CM dicusses safety of female college students with their representatives

tldr: Student leaders from women's colleges met the Delhi CM about dark roads, metro exits and PG areas they feel unsafe in.
